paper_id: Gong et al. - 2013 - Informative counting fine-grained batch authentication for large-scale RFID systems
title: Informative Counting: Fine-grained Batch Authentication for Large-Scale RFID Systems
motivation: Counterfeiting costs >600B yearly; deterministic per-tag auth too expensive for fast-moving consumer goods (clothes, wines)
problem_framing: Prior batch auth only yields binary 0/1 result; need scalable fine-grained count estimation for counterfeit and genuine tags
key_insight: Extend FM-Sketch into Authentication Synopsis; geometric-hash slot occupancy reveals |C| and |G| via set-difference ratio
method_signature: AS-based batch auth achieving O(N/n·log N) sublinear cost with (ε,δ) approximations
evaluation_criteria: Relative error |θ̂-θ|/θ ≤ ε with prob ≥ 1-δ; compare scanning slots and comm bytes vs ACTION/SEBA
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Sanity bound B is pessimistic due to worst-case analysis; may need extra round for undecided singleton slots
evidence_for_taste: approximate count of counterfeits and genuines with accuracy and error probability guarantees
result is binary, merely indicating the existence of counterfeits
the possibility of this luck is rather small and negligible
our analysis are based on the worst-case analysis
